@annevk I guess HTML is already overloading `returnValue` on `BeforeUnloadEvent`, right? Do we need to do anything more to call that out?

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#the-beforeunloadevent-interface

I don't think so. @domenic would know.

The current text looks good to me, but it's also starting to show that we don't use internal slots to back the event attributes. As now we have to initialize two attributes rather than a single slot that backs both of them.

You're still planning on adding `window.event`, right?
No need to do anything else, yeah.
Thats a perfect sort of thing

Is this PR in a state that I should try to write Gecko code for?

@hsivonen I had another look and while I thought I only had nits, I think one problem with `window.event` is that "If event's target's root is not a shadow root" is a runtime check, while this should be based on information known prior to dispatch. And perhaps we should also hide the event if any of its relatedTarget or touch target list contain shadow tree entries, but only while calling listeners in the shadow tree. (See also #585.)

`returnValue` should be safe to implement though and `srcElement` is already in Nightly.

> while this should be based on information known prior to dispatch.

Yeah, this definitely. Should also make the implementation faster, at least in Gecko.

But why is the check based on target and not currentTarget? I would have expected window.event to be null/undefined whenever an event listener in shadow DOM tries to access it. I think that makes the feature easier to understand - it works only in light DOM, and scripts in shadow DOM can't use it.

> But why is the check based on target and not currentTarget?

This... is a really good point.

We now have #626 for srcElement and returnValue so let's focus this PR on window.event. I rebased and dropped the other attributes, but I haven't addressed the issues with the current window.event setup yet. Since this seems to be somewhat of a priority I'm going to try help out with this PR.

I fixed a couple of things, including how to get a hold of the Window object.

The main thing I'm not sure how to do with the current setup is taking shadow trees into account. Currently we only store closed shadow tree information in the path. @smaug---- I guess Firefox stores more somehow?
(On IRC Olli pointed out this would require an additional bit on the path.)

Created extra tests: https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/pull/10329.

The only thing I haven't tested (apart from more exhaustive tests I suppose) is microtask callbacks and see whether window.event is set in them.

It seems that target's relevant global object might not be entirely correct either. If you do `document.appendChild(otherWindow.document.createElement("..."))` and dispatch an event on the return value it'll be `window.event` and not `otherWindow.event` that reflects it. So maybe if target is in a document we need to use the node document's relevant global object? So weird.

I've now updated this PR to use the suggestion from @yuki3 to take the global from the listener's callback. So now it's evaluated on a per-listener basis rather than on a per-event-target basis. Apologies for the delay. I'll next update the tests and file implementation bugs.
